subject: Re: Temporary throughput lift — surge credit ladder & commit alternatives
messages:
From: Alyssa Chen <alyssa@bluepine.io>
To: markus_klein@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@bluepine.io
Date: 2027-10-28T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Short-term capacity bump for launch next week

Markus —

Quick note from our side: we have a marketing-driven feature toggle going live Monday that will spike inference traffic for ~72 hours. We currently sit under your committed tier but the expected burst is ~3x our usual peak.

We need a short-term headroom option (1–3 days) and clarity on how overrun will be billed — specifically:
- Can you provide a temporary rate-limit increase or an ephemeral credit ladder?
- Would a partial commit bump (1 month) get us a discounted overrun rate?
- Any procurement/PO steps required to make this happen fast?

Significant if we can avoid throttling; can onboard a PO if needed.

Thanks,
Alyssa
Senior Product Manager
BluePine

---
Attachment: traffic-snapshot.png (image/png)
From: markus_klein@redwood.com
To: Alyssa Chen <alyssa@bluepine.io>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2027-10-28T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Short-term capacity bump for launch next week

Alyssa — thanks for the heads up and congrats on the launch. We can cover this, and there are two pragmatic paths so you don't get throttled:

1) Ephemeral surge credits (fastest): we provision a short-window headroom and apply a graded credit ladder — the first 24h of overrun billed at list, 24–48h discounted at 30%, 48–72h discounted at 50%. We can cap total charge if you give a PO.

2) Short-term commit (recommended if you plan recurring spikes): a 1-month temporary commit that lowers the per-token overrun rate by ~40% for the commit tier; we can backdate the effective time to cover the launch window if procurement is quick.

Ben — can you sketch numbers for both options (example: expected 3x peak = ~18M extra tokens/day) and include any quick legal/PO language?
Laura — please confirm billing/procurement lead time if they route a PO today.

I'll hold a 2-hour warm pool window on our side for Monday morning at your target RTP. If you want DocuSign, we can attach the SLA addendum and surge schedule.

—Markus
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference

---
Attachment: none
From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: markus_klein@redwood.com, Alyssa Chen <alyssa@bluepine.io>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2027-10-28T13:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Short-term capacity bump for launch next week

Alyssa / Markus —

Draft numbers below based on the 18M extra tokens/day estimate Mark called out. I modeled two scenarios and included a blended surge-credit CSV (attached).

Option A — Ephemeral Surge Credit Ladder (no commit)
- 0–24h: billed at standard overrun rate ($0.00012/token)
- 24–48h: 30% discount ($0.000084/token)
- 48–72h: 50% discount ($0.00006/token)
- Cap: if BluePine signs PO with amount >= $25k, cap total charge at $35k for the 72h window.

Option B — 1-month Temporary Commit (effective for calendar month)
- Temporary committed monthly spend: $45k (covers projected launch + buffer)
- Overrun beyond temporary commit: $0.000045/token (~40% below list)
- Benefit: lower per-token cost and we can retroactively apply the commit to the launch day if PO is approved within 48 hours.

Procurement path: fastest is an emailed PO referencing the SLA addendum and our procurement code. If you need our SOW/DocuSign template, I can push it now.

Next steps: Alyssa, tell us which option you prefer and whether you can route a PO today. If you say Option B, Laura will confirm invoice timing and whether we can bill pro rata for the temporary month.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Ben / Mark / Alyssa —

We can accept an emailed PO referencing the SLA addendum and the surge schedule. Timeline notes:
- If PO arrives before 48 hours from now, finance can create a proforma and we can apply a temporary commit effective the day of launch.
- Billing: we'll invoice the temporary commit pro rata for the remainder of the month; any cap/credit will appear as a line item on the following invoice.
- DocuSign: legal prefers the addendum attached to the existing MSA. Small redlines are okay but will add ~24 hours if present.

If BluePine wants the risk-minimal path with minimal procurement friction, Option A + PO for cap is the fastest. If you expect post-launch recurring spikes, Option B is cleaner financially.

Laura Bennett
Senior Finance Manager, Redwood Inference
